newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN criticises Taleban treatement of Afghan women.
newsitem.headline: UN criticises Taleban treatement of Afghan women.

text.p: The main U.N. human rights forum on Wednesday criticised Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban movement for excluding Afghan girls and women from basic education, training and employment.

The resolution adopted by consensus at the 53-member U.N. Human Rights Commisssion deplored human rights violations by the student militia movement, which captured the Afghan capital Kabul last September and now controls two-thirds of the war-ravaged country.

The Taleban, which has imposed tough Islamic Sharia laws across Afghanistan and banned women from leaving their homes without an all-covering Burqa veil, got rare praise from Pakistan at the Commission meeting in Geneva.

Pakistan, which has been supportive of the Taleban, told the forum ahead of the adoption of the resolution that the movement had promised to allow women back to work and to educate girls once peace and security were established throughout the country.
Led by their one-eyed leader Mollah Mohammed Umar, Taleban ousted a more moderate Islamic administration whose forces it is still fighting.
It has reopened Kabul university without female teachers or students. Anyone disobeying its orders is subjected to harsh punishment, which includes lashes at public places.
The U.N. resolution called for the immediate restoration of human rights of Afghan women in the workplace, schools and universities and their rights to freedom of movement.
It also voiced concern about an intensification of armed hostilities in Afghanistan which had led to forced evictions and destruction of houses on grounds of ethnicity.
